new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the second-to-last syllable of the word; no conditions, exceptions or examples are given.
new_statements.domain_note: Bare one-sentence statement in a standardised sketch format; domain (word vs phrase, citation form) not specified. The sketch says it is 'based on Charpentier (1979)', but Charpentier 1979 contains no stress statement, so this is Crowley's own addition (Williams 2019:17 calls the sketch a summary of Charpentier 'with some further notes on Lamap's phonology'); the source of the penult claim is not given.
new_statements.identity_note: Port Sandwich = Lamap = port1285 (ISO psw), the language of the Lamap area, SE Malakula. Crowley 2002 uses the toponym Port Sandwich for the same variety Charpentier 1979 and Williams 2019 describe ('Lamap'); no dialect distinction is made in any source. Not to be confused with the interior central-Malakula languages (Ayiaulian etc.) to which the Charpentier 1982a:63 'tonic accent on the next to last syllable' remark quoted in Lynch & Crowley 2001:71 refers.
